input.question: Why do lethal injections need to be sterilized?
input.ground_truth: Lethal injections are a medical procedure. Even if the intent is to kill the patient, it still must follow medical procedure. Mainly it's due to legal reasons. So if a man is sentenced to lethal injection and survives the injection, but then develops a serious infection that kills him, it also opens up a wrongful death lawsuit, since he was supposed to die from the injection, not the infection. Also since the injection isn't immediate, they insert the needle in his skin, if something happens, (power goes out, injection is delayed for whatever reason, governor calls with new evidence and a new trial is required) if the person gets an infection that opens up more legal repercussions.

Question: Why do lethal injections need to be sterilized?

Okay! Imagine you have a tiny cut on your finger. If you use a dirty bandage, germs can go into your cut and make you sick. 

Lethal injections are medicine that stops a person’s body from working. If the needle or the medicine is not clean (not sterilized), it can put yucky germs into the person’s body. Those germs can make them very sick or even cause them to die from something else, not just the medicine. 

So, we need to make sure everything is super clean (sterilized) so that only the medicine does its job, and no germs sneak in to hurt the person.
